name: Kinka
oneLiner: XNK is Kinka's gold-backed commodity token, with each token representing one troy ounce of 99.99% Japanese-brand gold bullion held with Loomis vaulting.
collateral: Each XNK represents one fine troy ounce equivalent of 99.99% Japanese-brand physical gold bullion held through Gold Management LLC and stored with Loomis International vaulting; issuer is Kinka (BVI) Ltd.
pegMechanism: XNK can be exchanged for physical gold through GM LLC/storage-company desks after AML/KYC; issuer docs describe a 321.5 XNK minimum for ten 1 kg bars, and secondary-market price tracks one fine troy ounce of gold.

mechanismArchetypeReview.rationale: Kinka's issuer whitepaper states that each XNK represents one troy fine ounce of 99.99% Japanese-brand physical gold, with bullion held at Loomis International and physical exchange through the issuer's disclosed redemption process. The reference is gold, not USD; fiat-cash is retained only as the repository's established fully-reserved commodity-token archetype, with commodityOunces carrying the operative claim measurement.

blacklistabilityReview.evidence: Kinka terms reserve issuer discretion over transfers and exchange and allow restrictions on Ethereum addresses; the centralized issuer and physical-gold redemption process create a direct blacklistability surface.

mintAuthority.summary: XNK uses an owner-controlled legacy mintable ERC-20; minting is not finished and the owner is a contract whose signer/threshold setup was not verified.

controls.label: XNK legacy mintable token
controls.evidence: Ethereum reads returned owner() = 0x2691FBB371456eaC5C5AA0082a0f53C91249c044 and mintingFinished() = false at block 25166611. Source review showed onlyOwner mint and finishMinting.

controls.label: XNK owner contract
controls.evidence: code read returned contract bytecode; no Safe threshold or owner model was verified.

review.evidence: XNK source/RPC reads show ongoing owner mint ability. Phase 0c follow-up: 0x2691FBB371456eaC5C5AA0082a0f53C91249c044 is a contract (22kb), not a Safe (Safe API 422, getOwners() reverts). owner() on 0x2691 returned 0x50ea796bcf3d178a100b1f0ef44faaef64741bfe (another contract, 22kb). 0x50ea is not a Safe (getOwners reverts, required() reverts). Neither contract exposes a legible multisig interface. The direct legacy token source does not identify a proxy or other code-replacement path, but its owner-control chain is unresolvable without verified source or ABI; cap, reconciliation, and supervision facts therefore remain unknown.
unresolvedQuestions: Resolve the admin/signature model for owner contract 0x2691FBB371456eaC5C5AA0082a0f53C91249c044 and its owner 0x50ea796bcf3d178a100b1f0ef44faaef64741bfe. Neither is a Safe or known multisig. Source code not verified on Sourcify or Etherscan. Cannot determine signer count or threshold.

reserves.name: Physical gold bullion (99.99% Japanese LBMA Good Delivery brands, Loomis/GM custody)
reserves.issuerOrObligor: Kinka (BVI) Ltd.; Gold Management LLC and Loomis International

reserveReview.rationale: Kinka documents XNK as representing 99.99% physical gold and describes redemption of 1 kg LBMA-hallmarked bars through Loomis International and affiliated warehouses after the published minimum holding threshold. The documents do not establish a redemption settlement time, so liquidity horizon remains unknown. The reserve is retained as one physical-gold slice; the medium risk classification reflects gold-market, issuer, custody, and physical-redemption exposure.
reserveReview.compositionBasis: Kinka physical-gold backing and redemption disclosures
reserveReview.knownUnknownExposure: The reviewed sources identify the physical-gold reserve and Loomis/Gold Management route but do not disclose bar-level inventory, account segregation, or current provider shares.

custodyProfile.uncertainty: Kinka describes Gold Management as legally independent from Kinka and its parent and says warehouse gold cannot be seized in their bankruptcy. The reviewed documents do not establish account-level segregation, rehypothecation safeguards, current custody shares, or a physical-redemption settlement time.

params.label: Physical gold bullion (99.99% Japanese LBMA Good Delivery brands)

bridgeRouteRisk.summary: XNK is reviewed as an issuer-native multichain token: supply is issued or redeemed by the issuer/operator on supported chains rather than through a separately identified third-party bridge token. Missing evidence for a public bridge lockbox keeps confidence below verified. The catalog's Cardano policy has no live asset record in Koios, so that individual route remains unresolved.
bridgeRouteRisk.reviewer: Codex bridge route review; Kimi P2 control cohort dc-6 (lead usde-ethena)

routes.reviewNote: XNK on Ethereum (owner() = 0x2691FBB371456eaC5C5AA0082a0f53C91249c044, mintingFinished() = false per the mint-authority review, re-confirmed 2026-07-20): Kinka's legacy owner-controlled mintable token. The owner contract chain (0x2691 → 0x50ea) remains unresolvable (see mint-authority review), but no third-party bridge mints this deployment — minting is owner-only on Ethereum.

routes.protocol: Kinka native XNK on Cardano (PlutusV3 minting policy)
routes.reviewNote: Resolved 2026-07-20. The earlier pass queried Koios with the whole 63-character catalog string as the policy id, which returns nothing; that string is actually the full Cardano asset unit, i.e. the 56-character policy id 2c5c6ca6f993e198bc9ac859ffb624dd291ec50b4d361544bd01e3ac followed by asset name 584e4b, which decodes to ASCII 'XNK'. Queried correctly, Koios policy_asset_info returns fingerprint asset1rvj40wqtucwlw6tzz4gs7080g02pm370z899m7, total_supply 167000000 raw units (167.0 XNK at 6 decimals), mint_cnt 1, burn_cnt 0, minting tx fdda5a1033250b95fa90051212be7273fc4729bde128e6639863868d181111ae, creation_time 1745226497, and Cardano token-registry metadata pointing to the issuer site kinka-gold.com. Koios script_info shows the policy id is itself a PlutusV3 script (creation tx bca0d497b8938bdfcd8fc2c82be36ffc478ba78bf7b74899f0f742b6f13abd60) whose decompiled text references a cold reference datum and NFT-gated policy checks, so minting is authorised by holding a specific policy NFT rather than by a plain key. This is therefore an issuer-native Cardano mint, not a third-party bridge representation: no lock-and-mint or burn-and-mint linkage to the Ethereum deployment exists, and the two supplies are independent (Ethereum totalSupply was 315.0 XNK at block 25575184 on the same day). The holder of the authorising policy NFT could not be enumerated from public indexer reads, so no controllerAddress is asserted.
